title: Completion of a lattice monoid as supported formal series
statement: Let $r\geq0$, let $M\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ be an additive subgroup, and put $Q=M\cap\mathbf N^r$, viewed as an additive monoid. Assume $Q$ is finitely generated. Let $L$ be a commutative local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and assume that the canonical map $L\to\varprojlim_a L/\mathfrak m^a$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $L[Q]$ for the ring of finite sums $\sum_q c_qz^q$, with $z^qz^{q\prime}=z^{q+q\prime}$, and put $J=\mathfrak m L[Q]+(z^q:q\in Q\setminus\{0\})$. Let $T=\varprojlim_a L[Q]/J^a$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ the formal power-series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The homomorphism $L[Q]\to A$, $z^q\mapsto X^q$, extends uniquely to an injective continuous $L$-algebra homomorphism $\iota:T\to A$, where $A$ has the $(\mathfrak m A+(X_1,\ldots,X_r))$-adic topology. Its image is exactly $A_Q=\{\sum_e c_eX^e:c_e=0\text{ for }e\notin Q\}$. The coefficient projection $\pi:A\to A_Q$, $\sum_e c_eX^e\mapsto\sum_{e\in Q}c_eX^e$, is additive, fixes $A_Q$ pointwise, and satisfies $\pi(ab)=a\pi(b)$ for every $a\in A_Q$ and $b\in A$. Thus $\rho=\iota^{-1}\pi:A\to T$ is a $T$-linear map with $\rho\iota=\operatorname{id}_T$.

proof.text: Put $B=L[Q]$ and $I=\mathfrak mA+(X_1,\ldots,X_r)A$. The basis map $j:B\to A$, $z^q\mapsto X^q$, preserves products because exponents add; distinct basis exponents give distinct series coefficients, so it is injective [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $|e|=\sum_i e_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $\Lambda=L$, base ideal $\mathfrak m$ and $d=r$: $F\in I^n$ precisely when $c_e(F)\in\mathfrak m^{n-|e|}$ for every $|e|<n$. This statement assumes neither Noetherianity nor completeness, so it applies to the given $L$.

source.place: Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), motivating context for the existing agent-formulated coefficient-criterion node; its full statement, including no Noetherianity requirement, is used.

proof.text: Choose nonzero generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$ and let $D=\max(1,|q_1|,\ldots,|q_s|)$; when $Q=\{0\}$ take the empty list and $D=1$. Put $E_n=j^{-1}(I^n)$. Since $j(J)\subseteq I$, $J^n\subseteq E_n$. Conversely take $f=\sum c_qz^q\in E_{Dn}$. Express $q$ with $h$ generator factors, so $|q|\leq Dh$. If $h\geq n$, its monomial already belongs to $J^n$. If $h<n$, the coefficient criterion gives $c_q\in\mathfrak m^{Dn-|q|}$, and $Dn-|q|\geq D(n-h)\geq n-h$; hence $c_qz^q\in J^{n-h}J^h=J^n$. Summing the finitely many terms proves $E_{Dn}\subseteq J^n$. These estimates include $q=0$, with $h=0$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: For $x=(x_n)_n\in T$ choose a polynomial representative $f_n\in B$ of $x_n\in B/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Compatibility gives $f_m-f_n\in J^n$ for $m\geq n$. By step 2 and the coefficient criterion, $c_e(jf_m)-c_e(jf_n)\in\mathfrak m^{n-|e|}$ whenever $n>|e|$. For each $k\geq1$ the residue of $c_e(jf_n)$ modulo $\mathfrak m^k$ is thus independent of $n\geq k+|e|$. These residues form a compatible system. The assumed bijection $L\to\varprojlim L/\mathfrak m^k$ supplies a unique $c_e(x)\in L$ with these residues. Changing representatives changes no stabilized residue. Thus $\iota(x)=\sum_e c_e(x)X^e$ is well defined as a series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: The construction gives $c_e(\iota x)-c_e(jf_n)\in\mathfrak m^{n-|e|}$ for $|e|<n$, hence $\iota x-jf_n\in I^n$ by the coefficient criterion. Representatives for $x+y$, $xy$ are $f_n+g_n$, $f_ng_n$. For fixed exponent $e$ and $k$, take $n\geq k+|e|$: every coefficient of exponent at most $e$ agrees with its limit modulo $\mathfrak m^k$. The finite convolution formula then shows $c_e(\iota(xy))$ and $\sum_{a+b=e}c_a(\iota x)c_b(\iota y)$ agree modulo every $\mathfrak m^k$, so they agree in $L$; the same computation with addition proves additivity. Here $\bigcap_k\mathfrak m^k=0$ follows from injectivity of the assumed completion map. Constant representatives prove preservation of $1$ and $L$, and $\iota|_B=j$. Thus $\iota$ is an $L$-algebra homomorphism.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: If $\iota x=0$, the preceding approximation at index $Dn$ gives $jf_{Dn}\in I^{Dn}$, and step 2 gives $f_{Dn}\in J^n$. Since $f_{Dn}$ represents $x_{Dn}$ and $x$ is compatible, its image modulo $J^n$ is $x_n=0$. This holds for every $n$, so $x=0$ as a compatible family. Therefore $\iota$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: For $e\notin Q$, every $jf_n$ has zero $e$-coefficient; hence $c_e(x)=0$, so $\iota(T)\subseteq A_Q$. Conversely let $F=\sum_{q\in Q}c_qX^q\in A_Q$. Let $b_n=\sum_{q\in Q,\ |q|<Dn}c_qz^q\in B$, a finite sum since $r$ is finite. If $m\geq n$, $j(b_m-b_n)$ has no terms below degree $Dn$, so it lies in $I^{Dn}$ by the coefficient criterion; step 2 gives $b_m-b_n\in J^n$. Thus $x_n=b_n\bmod J^n$ is a compatible family defining $x\in T$. For each $q$, the coefficient of $jb_n$ eventually equals $c_q$ exactly, so the construction of $\iota$ gives $\iota x=F$. This proves $\iota(T)=A_Q$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: Give $T=\varprojlim B/J^n$ its completion topology, with basic neighborhoods $P_n=\ker(T\to B/J^n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If $x\in P_n$, its representative $f_n$ is in $J^n$, so $jf_n\in I^n$; the approximation in step 4 then gives $\iota x\in I^n$. Thus $\iota$ is continuous. For any $x\in T$, the canonical image of $f_n$ differs from $x$ by an element of $P_n$, so these images converge to $x$. Also $A$ is separated for $I$: if $F\in\bigcap_nI^n$, its $e$-coefficient lies in every $\mathfrak m^k$ by taking $n=k+|e|$, hence is zero. Any other continuous extension of $j$ therefore has the same limit on the $f_n$, proving uniqueness.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: The set $A_Q$ is a subalgebra: $0\in Q$ and $Q+Q\subseteq Q$, so the finite coefficient convolution of two supported series again has support in $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Define $\pi$ coefficientwise as in the statement. Additivity and $\pi|_{A_Q}=1$ follow coefficientwise. For $a\in A_Q$, compute the $u$-coefficient using the finite sum over $q+e=u$. If $u\in Q$, every contributing $q$ lies in $Q$ and $e=u-q\in M\cap\mathbf N^r=Q$, so $\pi(ab)$ and $a\pi(b)$ have the same coefficient. If $u\notin Q$, the first coefficient is zero and the second is zero too: a nonzero contributing term would require $q,e\in Q$, forcing $u=q+e\in Q$. Thus $\pi(ab)=a\pi(b)$ for all $u$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 specifies the monoid models; Q09 agent argument for the auxiliary supported-series comparison.

proof.text: The proved injectivity and image equality make $\iota:T\to A_Q$ an $L$-algebra isomorphism. Put $\rho=\iota^{-1}\pi$. For $t\in T$ and $b\in A$, step 8 gives $\pi(\iota(t)b)=\iota(t)\pi(b)$; applying $\iota^{-1}$ gives $\rho(\iota(t)b)=t\rho(b)$. Additivity transports in the same way, proving $T$-linearity. Finally $\pi\iota=\iota$ gives $\rho\iota=\operatorname{id}_T$.
